events.title: Economics may decide outcome of Iran-US standoff
events.summary: The next phase of the Iran–US standoff may be decided not on the battlefield, but by how much economic pressure each side can withstand.

events.title: United States Condemns the Pro-Hamas Global Sumud Flotilla
events.summary: The United States condemns the Global Sumud Flotilla, a pro-Hamas initiative and a baseless, counterproductive effort to undermine President Trump’s Peace Plan. This Pro-Hamas Flotilla is organized by an OFAC-sanctioned entity, the Popular Conference for Palestinians Abroad, which was designated as a specially designated global terrorist in January for operating at Hamas’ behest. The founder of the Global Sumud Flotilla has publicly expressed support for the Iranian regime and its terror proxies

events.title: Pezeshkian, Ghalibaf seek Araghchi’s ouster over 'subservience' to Guards
events.summary: Iran's president and parliament speaker are seeking Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi’s removal, accusing him of following the Revolutionary Guard chief’s instructions in nuclear talks without informing the president, two sources familiar with the matter told Iran International.

events.title: US forms new coalition to secure Hormuz, asks partners to join
events.summary: The United States has asked partner countries to join its newly formed Maritime Freedom Coalition to help secure passage through the Strait of Hormuz and Persian Gulf waterways, according to a State Department cable.

events.title: Iranians denounce tiered internet plan as discriminatory and corrupt
events.summary: Iranians condemned selective access to restricted internet services as discriminatory and corrupt in messages to Iran International, urging others to reject the scheme in recent days.

events.title: How the Taliban tilted toward Iran during wartime tensions
events.summary: Taliban leaders and affiliated figures voiced support for Iran after Israeli strikes in June 2025 and later US threats, signaling a limited and conditional alignment despite longstanding disputes with Tehran.

events.title: Iran ranks near bottom as press curbs deepen worldwide
events.summary: Iran ranked among the world’s worst countries for press freedom in 2026 as global conditions hit a 25-year low, with legal pressure on journalists intensifying across multiple regions, Reporters Without Borders said.

events.title: Soaring prices push medicine beyond Iranians' reach
events.summary: Medicine prices in Iran have surged sharply in recent weeks, with some drugs rising by as much as 380%, according to reports received by Iran International, as the country grapples with soaring inflation, a collapsing currency and worsening wartime disruption.

events.title: As Tehran praises Moscow, critics ask where Russia was
events.summary: As Iranian officials continue to tout a “strategic partnership” with Russia, rare public criticism has emerged over Moscow’s muted response to the recent war.

events.title: Secretary Rubio’s Call with German Foreign Minister Wadephul
events.summary: The below is attributable to Spokesperson Tommy Pigott: Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke today with German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul on the ongoing situation with Iran. The Secretary and Foreign Minister discussed the security situation in the region and underscored the importance of securing freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.

events.title: Iran football chief with IRGC ties sent back by Canada after arrival
events.summary: Iran's football chief Mehdi Taj, once a commander in the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, was sent back from Canada just hours after landing, according to a government source who spoke to Iran International.

events.title: Secretary Rubio’s Meeting with UK Foreign Secretary Cooper
events.summary: The below is attributable to Spokesperson Tommy Pigott: Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with UK Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper on the occasion of King Charles III and Queen Camilla’s visit to the United States.  The Secretary and Foreign Secretary discussed the urgent need to restore freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.

events.title: Even state media sounds alarm as Iran’s economy sinks
events.summary: Iran’s worsening economic crisis is drawing unusually blunt warnings from state media and establishment voices as war, inflation and shortages squeeze households and expose the limits of the government’s response.

events.title: Iran currency plunges as dollar crosses 1.8 million in open market
events.summary: The US dollar passed 1.81 million rials on Iran’s open market on Wednesday, rising nearly 8% in a single day as the country’s economic crisis worsened under the strain of maritime blockade, stalled diplomacy and mounting pressure on households.

events.title: Tehran is pricing out its daughters
events.summary: For years, young women from smaller cities and conservative families came to Tehran to study, to work, to breathe. Now, one by one, many are being forced to leave.

events.title: Iran war clouds summer travel as jet fuel costs soar
events.summary: European airlines are facing their biggest test since the COVID-19 pandemic as the Iran war drives up jet fuel prices, disrupts Middle East routes and raises concerns about possible fuel shortages ahead of the summer holiday season.

events.title: Iran taps reserves again as inflation bites and layoffs mount
events.summary: Iran has once again tapped its sovereign wealth reserves to fund essential imports, highlighting the growing strain on an economy battered by war, inflation and a rapidly weakening currency.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz coalition forms
threads.summary: The US State Department asked partner countries to join a newly formed Maritime Freedom Coalition to secure passage through the Strait of Hormuz, according to a department cable. Secretary Rubio raised freedom of navigation in calls with UK Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper and German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul.

threads.label: Iran economic crisis deepens
threads.summary: The US dollar passed 1.81 million rials on Iran's open market, medicine prices rose by as much as 380%, and Tehran tapped sovereign wealth reserves again to fund essential imports. Iran International reported state media issuing unusually blunt warnings about war, inflation and shortages, with the standoff increasingly framed in economic terms.

threads.label: Tehran political infighting and foreign alignments
threads.summary: Iran International reported that President Pezeshkian and parliament speaker Ghalibaf are seeking Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi's removal, citing two sources who accused him of following IRGC instructions in nuclear talks. Separate reports examined Taliban figures voicing support for Iran after the June 2025 Israeli strikes, and rare domestic criticism of Russia's muted wartime response.

threads.label: Civil liberties and rights inside Iran
threads.summary: Reporters Without Borders ranked Iran among the worst countries for press freedom in 2026 as global conditions hit a 25-year low, while Iranians told Iran International a tiered internet access scheme was discriminatory. Labour MP Ruth Jones tabled a written question to the FCDO on the impact of restricted education, employment and public services on the Bahá'í community and other minorities.

threads.label: US pressure on Hamas-linked flotilla and IRGC figure
threads.summary: The State Department condemned the Global Sumud Flotilla, noting it is organised by the OFAC-designated Popular Conference for Palestinians Abroad, sanctioned in January as a specially designated global terrorist for operating at Hamas's behest. Iran International reported that Iran's football chief Mehdi Taj, a former IRGC commander, was sent back from Canada hours after landing, citing a government source.
